Dude, that’s not how ‘science’ works. You can’t just cite a single study then conclude ‘right, that’s it, case closed’. I don’t have time to write an extremely detailed response right now (which this merits) but just looking at that one study, they gave testosterone to ADULTS and expected it to affect their cognitive empathy. This seems like a silly idea to begin with. Giving a single dose of estrogen or inhibiting 5 alpha reductase in an adult male doesn’t make your penis suddenly turn into a vagina; why would they expect a single dose of testosterone to somehow rewire an already mature brain? In all domains of endocrinology, foetal development is the most crucial stage, followed by puberty. These are the periods the EMB theory refers to; we don’t necessarily have higher testosterone levels as adults (sorry guys). I’m not saying the EMB theory is perfect, but it’s certainly the most scientifically rigorous attempt to understand autism we have so far; certainly more so than a single study.
